record_summary: High-volume LLM workload with strong cost pressure. Interested in Redwood Dedicated, leaning Tier Plus to get a committed throughput floor + defined burst policy (they have predictable baseline plus periodic spikes). Wants concrete tokens/sec commitments by model + a clear explanation of how Redwood measures throughput for streaming outputs. Evaluating against Bedrock + existing vendor; open to model pinning and routing guardrails if it reduces cost volatility.
key_requirements: Workload: (1) video metadata + comment summarization (batch + near-real-time), (2) policy/moderation classification with strict latency at p95, (3) internal support-agent/search over help center. Volume: sustained high QPS during peak hours + event-driven bursts (launches, sports events). Latency: wants stable p95 and predictable queueing behavior under saturation (prefers admission control over silent tail latency). Throughput: wants an explicit committed throughput floor per deployment, and a burst allowance with defined limits + overage pricing/metering. Models: prefers open models (Llama 3.x class for chat/summarization; smaller model for moderation/classification), wants ability to pin model version for at least a quarter and do controlled rollouts. Context: mix of short (chat/modeation) and long context for summarization; needs guidance on max context and batching recommendations by shape. Observability: customer-visible dashboard or export for throughput vs commitment; wants incident postmortems when SLO is missed. Security: VPC deployment, KMS integration, audit logs, retention controls; no strict on-prem requirement.

notes_internal: Positioning: emphasize Dedicated Tier Plus = committed throughput floor + defined burst pool behavior, with tier-aware admission control to protect baseline. They are allergic to 'up to' language without measurement details. They asked specifically how we compute tokens/sec when streaming (they previously saw mismatched dashboards from another vendor). Simran to coordinate with SRE/Obs on the customer-safe wording + reporting screenshots. Likely best fit: a standard shape in us-east with capacity headroom to handle routine bursts; ensure we don’t promise cross-region failover beyond Tier Premium. Pricing: they will push for aggressive discounting; route through Deal Desk early and keep to guardrails.

open_questions: Exact burst envelope requested: % over commit and duration (need them to confirm: e.g., 2x for 30 minutes vs 1.25x for 4 hours).
Which primary model(s) they will pin for the committed throughput calculation (single-model vs multi-model deployment).
Whether they require customer-visible SLO reporting in Console at GA or can start with weekly exports during POC.
proposed_solution_draft: Dedicated Tier Plus in us-east. Commit a throughput floor for the pinned model + context class; enable tier-aware routing and admission control to cap queue growth under saturation. Offer burst with explicit cap and metering (separate line item / usage export). Provide a lightweight reporting pack: daily throughput vs commitment + saturation signals, with clear exclusions (customer throttling, unsupported model/version, warmup window).
deal_risk: Medium: strong fit technically but price sensitive; will stall if burst policy language is ambiguous or if we can’t demonstrate measurement/auditability for streaming throughput.
